Naturalism is the broader thesis that the natural world, studied through scientific methods, is the only proper basis for understanding everything, including human affairs, and that philosophy should not claim a separate, supernatural, or "first philosophy" foundation. Positivism is a narrower doctrine within that outlook, holding that meaningful knowledge must rest on empirically verifiable observation and rejecting metaphysics and untestable claims. So positivism is best read as one strict form of naturalism, and naturalism can accept theoretical entities and philosophy that positivism would reject.
